Question
========
Besides `carat`, `cut`, `color` and `price`, the `diamonds` dataset also contains three columns describing a diamond's physical dimensions in millimeters: `x` (length), `y` (width) and `z` (depth). Right now, these three measurements are stored in wide format - one column each.

Write R code using `pivot_longer()` from the `tidyr` package that reshapes `diamonds` into long format with respect to these three columns, so that the result has a column called `Dimension` holding the name of the measurement (`"x"`, `"y"` or `"z"`) and a column called `Length_mm` holding the corresponding value.


Solution
========
```
library(tidyr)

diamonds_long <- pivot_longer(
  diamonds,
  cols = x:z,
  names_to = "Dimension",
  values_to = "Length_mm"
)
```

`cols = x:z` selects the three columns to reshape, `names_to = "Dimension"` tells `pivot_longer()` to store the original column names (`"x"`, `"y"`, `"z"`) in a new column called `Dimension`, and `values_to = "Length_mm"` stores the corresponding measurements in a new column called `Length_mm`. All other columns, such as `carat`, `cut` and `price`, are kept as they are and simply repeated for each of the three measurements belonging to a diamond - which is exactly the long format ggplot2 would need if, for example, you wanted to compare the three dimensions in a single faceted plot.
